name: Auriga
introduction: is the Charioteer, often drawn carrying a goat and her kids on his arm. Its bright stars form a large pentagon, high overhead on northern winter evenings, with brilliant golden Capella at one corner.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Capella](hip:24608), the sixth-brightest star in the sky, is not one star but two yellow giants, each about ten times wider than the Sun, orbiting each other every 104 days, about 43 light-years away. A distant pair of red dwarfs belongs to the same system. Its name means “little she-goat”.

Nearby, a small triangle of stars represents the goat’s kids. One of them, Epsilon Aurigae, is among the strangest eclipsing binaries known: every 27 years, a huge, dark disk of dust passes in front of its supergiant star, dimming it for nearly two years.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Menkalinan](hip:28360) is an eclipsing binary of two similar stars that dims slightly every four days. [Saclateni](hip:23453), also called Zeta Aurigae, is another eclipsing pair, an orange giant with a blue companion that disappears behind it every 2.7 years.
[Elnath](hip:25428), the tip of Taurus’s horn, is also part of the pentagon and was once shared between the two constellations. [Mahasim](hip:28380) and [Hassaleh](hip:23015) complete the figure.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Milky Way runs through Auriga, which contains three bright open clusters, M36, M37 and M38, within reach of binoculars. The Flaming Star Nebula glows around AE Aurigae, a runaway star flung out of the Orion Nebula region about two million years ago.
